summary: Added two @pytest.mark.deepagent integration tests to tests/test_deep_agent_integration.py:

test_post_completion_guard_through_deep_agent: 4-step scripted model sequence (begin_work → complete_pipeline → get_next_action → final text); verifies post-completion guard intercepts ledger_get_next_action after completion and returns WAIT without calling the original coroutine (gna_calls==0).

test_error_rollback_cancels_pipeline_through_deep_agent: 2-step scripted model sequence (begin_work → crash_tool); crash_tool raises RuntimeError which propagates through Deep Agents to create_stage_node's except block; rollback fires and calls ledger_cancel_pipeline with auto_cancelled=True; verified via cp_calls capturing.

Added _make_cancel_pipeline_tool helper: installs a capture wrapper below the framework wrappers (inject_project_path, restrict_to_wp) to record the raw ainvoke input dict before LangChain schema short-circuits _AnyArgsSchema to **{}, ensuring auto_cancelled=True is verifiable.

comments.note: test_deep_agent_integration.py: _make_cancel_pipeline_tool uses object.__setattr__ to install a capture wrapper below the framework wrappers. This pattern is consistent with how the production code (_patch_tool, _install_tracker) bypasses Pydantic __setattr__. It is safe and intentional, but worth noting for future readers.

test_deep_agent_integration.py: the crash_tool exception propagation behavior (RuntimeError escapes Deep Agents' ToolNode) was empirically confirmed and is not documented in Deep Agents 0.5.2 public docs. If a future Deep Agents release adds handle_tool_errors=True to its ToolNode, test_error_rollback_cancels_pipeline_through_deep_agent could silently break. Consider adding a version pin or a note in the test file if this behavior becomes unstable.

comments.note: test_error_rollback: crash_tool exception propagation through Deep Agents 0.5.2 ToolNode is empirically confirmed but undocumented. If a future Deep Agents release adds handle_tool_errors=True to its internal ToolNode (absorbing exceptions into ToolMessages rather than propagating them), the rollback test would silently break — the RuntimeError would no longer reach create_stage_node's except block. A version pin comment or a note in the test's docstring would help future maintainers detect this.

_make_cancel_pipeline_tool uses object.__setattr__ to install an ainvoke capture wrapper, bypassing Pydantic's __setattr__. This is consistent with _patch_tool / _install_tracker patterns in production code (src/nodes.py). The technique is intentional and safe here, but the workaround depends on StructuredTool not using __slots__ — worth a brief comment in the helper.

summary: Code review PASS — both WP-005 tests and the _make_cancel_pipeline_tool helper are sound.

test_post_completion_guard_through_deep_agent: clean and correct. The gna_calls==0 assertion is the right proof: zero original-coroutine invocations is only possible if the guard intercepted the call and returned the synthetic WAIT response. stage_success=True confirms the agent completed the loop normally after receiving WAIT.

test_error_rollback_cancels_pipeline_through_deep_agent: correctly captures auto_cancelled=True via _make_cancel_pipeline_tool which installs its ainvoke wrapper BEFORE create_stage_node's own wrappers, placing it innermost in the chain. The flat-dict and ToolCall-structure branches in the capture wrapper are both handled. The empirically-confirmed Deep Agents 0.5.2 exception propagation behavior is documented in the test docstring — this is the key design assumption to preserve.

Documentation-forward: the Deep Agents version dependency for RuntimeError propagation should be made more explicit with a version pin comment or conftest note to prevent silent breakage if a future release adds handle_tool_errors=True to its ToolNode.

comments.note: _make_cancel_pipeline_tool correctly sits at the innermost position in the wrapper chain (installed before create_stage_node applies inject_project_path and restrict_to_wp), so it sees the final dict after all outer wrappers. The comment in the helper explains this correctly. One subtlety: the technique works because object.__setattr__ on StructuredTool (a Pydantic BaseModel subclass without __slots__) allows overwriting attribute descriptors. If LangChain migrates StructuredTool to use __slots__ and 'ainvoke' is not in them, this would fail. A brief comment noting the Pydantic/no-slots dependency in the helper would help future maintainers.

[documentation-forward] test_error_rollback_cancels_pipeline_through_deep_agent relies on RuntimeError propagating out of Deep Agents 0.5.2's internal ToolNode (exceptions are not wrapped in ToolMessage). This behavior is empirically confirmed but not documented in Deep Agents public docs. The test docstring already mentions this (Empirically confirmed with Deep Agents 0.5.2), but the version reference should be made explicit with a version pin comment alongside the deepagents import or in a conftest note. If a future Deep Agents release adds handle_tool_errors=True to its ToolNode, the RuntimeError would be absorbed into a ToolMessage and the rollback test would silently pass a green result while the production behavior changed.

test_post_completion_guard: gna_calls==0 is a strong guarantee — it proves the guard returned the synthetic WAIT response AND the original coroutine was never invoked. This is the correct assertion for this behavior. No change needed.
